# make-localllm-easier

> One command (`localllm`) that picks, downloads and runs the most accurate local LLM for a PC's GPU and the user's language, chosen from measured benchmark scores, with llama.cpp tuned for AMD, NVIDIA, Intel and Apple GPUs. MIT license. Python CLI on PyPI: `pip install make-localllm-easier`.

## Use
- `localllm`: detect GPU/RAM, pick model, download llama.cpp + model, start an OpenAI-compatible server at http://127.0.0.1:8080/v1, open chat page
- `localllm doctor`: which model sizes (4B-120B MoE) fit this GPU, at which quantization, estimated speed, context capacity
- `localllm chat`: chat in the terminal with streaming and history; `/attach FILE|FOLDER` answers from PDF, DOCX, TXT or MD files with the passages listed as sources (indexed on the PC, CPU-only embeddings)
- `localllm eval --langs en,ja`: multiple-choice accuracy of any OpenAI-compatible server (Global-MMLU-Lite 23 languages, INCLUDE 44 countries, ThaiExam); `--suites math` adds MGSM math word problems in 11 languages; `--suites translate` adds FLORES-101 translation (chrF++) in 101 languages
- `localllm --ui`: local chat page with saved chats, model picker, live VRAM/RAM; nothing loaded from the internet
- `--profile lean|max`: lean (default) = 8k context, ~2 GB RAM; max = context that fills the GPU (~78k on 16 GB) for agents
- `localllm connect hermes|opencode|claude-code|codex|aider|cline|obsidian`: point a tool at the local endpoint, `--undo` restores
- `localllm savings`: tokens answered locally this month, prompt-cache reuse, $ at user-set prices
- `localllm eval --suites longctx`: needle retrieval at 8k/32k/64k tokens in en, th, hi, ar, zh, ja, es
- `localllm serve --models auto`: per-message routing between local models by measured language/task scores (opt-in; lazy-load on 16 GB, all resident on 24 GB+), answering model shown in the X-Localllm-Model header

## Key measured facts (RX 9070 XT 16 GB, Windows, llama.cpp Vulkan)
- Qwen3.8-27B UD-Q3_K_XL (12.2 GB): English 81.5% (Global-MMLU-Lite), ~50 tok/s with MTP drafting
- gemma-4-26B-A4B QAT Q4 (13.3 GB): English 82.2%, ~90 tok/s
- 2-bit quantization costs 8-13 points; Hindi, Arabic, Thai lose most (13)
- Language-specific imatrix calibration gives no gain at ~3.5 bits
- 2-bit per-language KL divergence vs Q8: 4-6x the 3-bit damage in every language; build 2-bit files from BF16, not Q8 (Thai -9 points)
- MGSM math: gemma-4-26B-A4B QAT 96.8 en / 89.6 th / 88.8 zh vs Qwen3.8-27B Q3 94.4 / 87.2 / 84.4
- AMD/Intel without Resizable BAR: set GGML_VK_DISABLE_HOST_VISIBLE_VIDMEM=1 for up to 1.7x decode (llama.cpp#27097)
